### Source-side problems found (reported, not re-judged against the documents)
- **P1 — retired clause still encoded by an un-retired parameter (policy side).** `charge_ext_response_relief_credit.overwrite[2]` retires "otherwise payments issued before the late response stay charged even if relief is later granted", but variant parameter `relief_bar_for_payments_before_late_response: true` (all seven variants, bound in `charge_evt_notice_and_response.params`) still states it. The KB carries both: notice_and_response_af685a20 "**no longer in force** ... it is not applied" vs notice_response_terms_8657c3d9 "Payments issued before a late response stay charged even if relief is later granted | Yes ×7" under "The terms below govern ...". This is the policy's own contradiction, faithfully exposed. It bears directly on this root policy's domain: for a response received late without good cause, the schedule row would cut payments issued before the response out of the relief, while the in-force relief answer share (0.90 / 0.75) is the replacement basis. No scored value moves in this task (the response is timely), so it is recorded, not used to re-judge the documents.
- No rule-vs-compute disagreement found in charge_ext_response_disputed_amount or charge_ext_response_relief_credit (checked tier by tier above; the reserve-credit count is exact because `taxacct_reserve_credited` always carries `contribution_paid`).
